plan.title: Melanoma anti-PD-1 immune/stromal composition from TPM
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 anti-PD-1 treated, 6 untreated melanoma biopsies), no raw counts. This forces limma-trend on log2(TPM+1) rather than a count model for any expression testing, and it means the composition question — the primary research question — is answered from a linear-scale TPM matrix that matches the reference profiles used by TPM-native deconvolution tools (EPIC, quanTIseq). The plan: (1) QC the sample structure on log2(TPM+1), explicitly inspecting the flagged low-depth sample (sample_01, ~1/4 median depth) rather than dropping it silently; (2) filter to genes at or above 1 TPM in at least 6 samples (the smaller group size); (3) run cell-type deconvolution through immunedeconv (EPIC and quanTIseq for absolute fractions, MCP-counter for relative abundance scores, xCell for 64-type enrichment scores, ConsensusTME for a cancer-type-matched microenvironment estimate) so that no single algorithm's idiosyncrasies drive a composition claim — a claim is only made where methods agree in direction; (4) cross-check the immune/stromal call with scGate's HiTME hierarchical marker gating as a descriptive, non-quantitative sanity check, since scGate was built for single-cell gating and its bulk application here is exploratory only; (5) test each cell-type estimate for a treated-vs-control difference with limma or a t-test on the score matrix (BH-adjusted across cell types), which is the correct unit of replication (one score per sample, not per gene); (6) run the standard limma-trend differential expression contrast (treated vs untreated, explicit reference level) so that a composition-driven gene (e.g. a T-cell marker) is not mistaken for a cell-intrinsic transcriptional change, and report the two side by side; (7) integrate into one report stating tool versions, the reference-tissue match caveat for EPIC/quanTIseq (blood/tumor-derived references applied to melanoma), CIBERSORT/ESTIMATE absence and their open-source substitutes, and the low-depth sample's effect on its own estimates. ESTIMATE and CIBERSORT are not available in this environment; EPIC/quanTIseq and xCell/ConsensusTME are named explicitly as the substitutes, and the report will not claim an LM22-proportion or a tumor-purity result that only those absent tools can produce.
